9135674699c4e987.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants the £18.40 in foreign transaction fees refunded and an apology for how he was treated on the phone. The file records no promise or commitment by the bank to the customer. The handler's note confirms six FX fees totalling £18.40, records that the tariff was set up wrongly, and says the call recording from 21/10 has been requested. These are internal findings and actions, not promises. Nothing in the file shows that a refund, an apology or any redress has been offered or agreed. Any decision on the outcome or redress is for an authorised handler (CH-8).

d6694d52a3da7794.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: FEE-6 applies: FX fees should not be charged on the Travel Card, so any such fee is a bank error and FEE-2 applies. FEE-2 requires a full refund of the fee plus any interest charged on it, and a goodwill payment in line with RED. The note confirms the tariff was set up wrongly. Because there is a staff conduct element, CH-6 makes a staff conduct complaint Medium severity. CH-7 needs one primary root cause tag. CH-2 requires logging and written acknowledgement within 3 business days. CH-4 requires a Final Response within 8 weeks. The upheld decision and any redress amount must be made by an authorised person (CH-8, RED-5). The file does not record whether an acknowledgement has been sent.
